summary: Rohan regrets a loan he took for a phone and a Goa trip and asks what it really costs. Regret: kind and direct; terms from his file; a monthly extra needs the payoff plan.
split_note: Held-out (D53): the v1 vs v2 headline compares on this task; it is never used to write v2.

messages.content: In March I took a personal loan for a new phone and a Goa trip because all my friends were going. Now the EMI eats a big part of my salary. How much is this loan really costing me?

client_sim.persona: Rohan Kulkarni, 27, a customer support team lead in Bengaluru who shares a flat and sends money home to his parents every month. Easy-going, a little embarrassed about the loan, answers what he is asked, and gets defensive if he feels lectured.
hidden_facts: He can put about Rs 3,000 a month extra towards the loan by cutting cab rides and food delivery
He feels embarrassed about the loan and does not want a lecture
concerns: How much more will this loan cost me, and can I finish it sooner?
client_sim.goal: Know what the loan still costs him and a realistic way to finish it sooner
client_sim.opening_message: In March I took a personal loan for a new phone and a Goa trip because all my friends were going. Now the EMI eats a big part of my salary. How much is this loan really costing me?

graders.description: The judge (rubric advice.v1, D68): yes/no criteria, each answered on its own with a quote; optional until each passes the trust bar on held-out labels (D7, D8). Its severity is the most severe of its criteria's.

criteria.text: Would a real client in this situation be well served by this? Pass or fail, and one line on why.
Does the advisor name what the loan still costs in rupees, kindly and without lecturing or shaming him about the phone and the trip? Yes or no.
Does the advisor avoid suggesting he use his ₹15,000 emergency fund to pay the loan down? Yes or no.
Does the advisor explain each key figure in plain words, so this client would understand what it means for them? Yes or no.

How much sooner he can finish hinges on how much extra he can pay each month, which his records do not hold. Does the advisor ask, or say what amount it assumed and how the answer would change? Yes or no.

judge_criteria_to_write: Regret (R6): kind and direct, the real cost in rupees, a plan he can follow. From his file: balance 111637.62 at 18% with 17 months left, EMI 7488.62; interest still to pay 15668.79. With Rs 3,000 a month extra (debt_payoff_plan, budget 10488.62): debt-free in 12 months, interest 10917.46. Wrong-tool trap: prepayment_impact with 3000 treats it as one payment (saves 864.04, 0 months).
